newsitem.title: USA: US W.Coast CARB gasoline gains amid supply drop.
newsitem.headline: US W.Coast CARB gasoline gains amid supply drop.

text.p: Prices for U.S. West Coast CARB gasoline rose sharply Tuesday after weekly inventory data confirmed that supply has been drained by regional exports and lower refinery output.
The wholesale price for state-mandated CARB gasoline rose $0.03 a gallon from Tuesday to 65/66 cents a gallon. Premium, or higher octane, grade stood $0.06 a gallon higher than regular grade.
Prices got a lift after the American Petroleum Institute, a key industry representative, reported West Coast supplies of gasoline fell 1.4 million barrels to 27.6 million last week.
"The market will probably stay solid for the next two weeks," one trader said.
A handful of refinery problems and rumors of shutdowns also forced buyers to raise their prices.
Traders said Chevron in Richmond, Calif., shut part of their gasoline-making unit, while Shell and Exxon were rumored to be returning from unit problems.
In addition, U.S. Northwest refiners, which cut runs earlier this month, were still slow to bring up production.
"You don't speed up that quickly. There's not a lot of confidence in this market's ability to sustain inself past mid-August," a Northwest refinery trader said.

Wholesale prices for U.S Northwest products have lifted southern markets, traders said. Traders said Tosco's northern California refineries fell short of gasoline supplies after shipping grades to Seattle and Vancouver.
ARCO's Cherry Point, Washington, refinery has also sent supplies north.
In Seattle, unleaded gasoline stood 63/64 cents a gallon.
"A couple million" barrels of gasoline have been shipped north the last month, traders said.
Other products rose one to two cents in line with broader market gains, traders said.
